description: THE RULE ITSELF, in the profile that claims none of these names. Declarations of names belonging to optional profiles -- Sprites, Interaction & Events, Geometry and Sound -- are checked under `profiles: ["core-language"]` alone, and every one raises `ol-reserved-word`. `spec/grammar.md:384`: "The grammar has exactly four declaration slots ... A built-in name in any of those slots raises `ol-reserved-word`. Nothing shadows", and `:410` supplies the reason a profile cannot soften it -- a program cannot declare which profiles it requires, so a name declarable under one profile set and not another would make conformance implementation-dependent, "invisible and unpredictable to a learner". This fixture lives under `core-language/` deliberately: the declaration rule is Core's rather than each profile's, so a Core-only program is the case that decides it, and removing the rule reddens a Core fixture rather than only profile ones. The declarations cross the predicate's internal branches rather than sampling one of them: `ask` and `when` are profile KEYWORDS (Sprites and Interaction & Events, from `OL_PROFILE_KEYWORDS`); `grid`, `new_turtle`, `wait` and `set_tempo` are registered PRIMITIVES of Geometry, Sprites, Interaction & Events and Sound, which reach the predicate through a different lookup; and `struct tell` uses the `struct` declaration slot rather than `define` -- `spec/grammar.md:167` makes them separate slots, so a change reaching only `define` would leave that line clean. `"check": true`: these are checker diagnostics -- nothing is called, no struct is instantiated, and no events are produced.
